abandon: m04 says RL's edge on misread steps grows with the step's distance from the problem statement, because the base's recall of the problem weakens as its own solution gets longer. The board already shows that the RL edge does not grow with distance. (1) result-a6ab7a reports 'RL's advantage is in the first half of the answer and is in the text by the halfway point'. The second half holds the steps farthest from the statement. There, given a sound prefix, the base finishes as well as RL: 'Right prefixes from 50 % on: both finish equally (83 vs 83 of 88 base prefixes; 131 vs 134 of 140 RL prefixes)'. On wrong prefixes the edge also disappears at the latest cut: '+5.7 [-2.9, 14.3] at 75 %'. The same item reports 'Refuted: 'late checking' (no RL edge at 75 %)'. Under m04 the base's recall is weakest in that region, so RL's edge should be largest there. It is zero. m04's holds_against answers result-a6ab7a only by saying distance can grow inside the first half. That does not explain why the edge is absent at the largest distances. (2) The errors sit near the statement, not far from it. result-afc423 reports 'First wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer'. result-faf15a locates the steps at a 'median 29 tokens' long, and result-5e17a6 finds the base's short answers mostly right ('Base answers <= 2,000 tokens: 263, 13 wrong'). (3) In-context reading does not separate the models where it was tested. result-c4411d: 'RL does not read partial results better (chains -0.007 [-0.04,0.03])'. result-abb853: 'every standard set equal' on the workspace and multihop tests. (4) The proposed base change does not test the mechanism. A restatement prefilled right after the cue sits about 100 tokens from the original statement, not 'close to the step', so it barely changes the distance the mechanism names. What result-faf15a does show (Math 3.1 lowers misreads, D -1.52) fits RL simply making fewer reading errors early in the answer, with no dependence on distance.
